instruction.text: Here is a square. The area of the large shaded triangle is double the area of the small shaded triangle. What fraction of the whole square is the shaded area?
Here is a regular hexagon. The area of one of the large shaded triangles is double the area of the small shaded triangle. What fraction of the whole hexagon is the shaded area?
Here are two equilateral triangles. The large unshaded triangle is 3 times bigger than the small shaded triangle. What fraction of the large triangle is the shaded area?
Here is a regular octagon. The area of the large shaded triangle is double the area of the small shaded triangle. What fraction of the whole octagon is the shaded area?
Here is a regular pentagon. The large unshaded triangle is double the area of the small unshaded triangle. What fraction of the whole pentagon is the shaded area?
Here is a regular pentagon. The quadrilateral is 2/5 of the pentagon. What fraction of the whole pentagon is the shaded area?

Here are three equilateral triangles within one another. The small triangle is 1/3 of the size of the medium triangle. The medium triangle is 1/3 of the size of the large triangle. What fraction of the large triangle is the shaded area?
Here is a regular hexagon. What fraction of the whole hexagon is the shaded area? Give your answer in its simplest form.
